table_title: List the world's 20 tallest completed man-made dams by structural height (foundation to crest, in metres) — with each dam's country, primary river dammed, and year of completion. Source universe is Wikipedia's 'List of tallest dams' master article, filtered to man-made dams (natural landslide/lava dams in the master table are excluded).
db_analog: SELECT d.dam_name AS dam, d.structural_height_m AS height, d.country, d.primary_river AS river, d.year_completed FROM dams d WHERE d.is_man_made = TRUE AND d.is_completed = TRUE AND d.height_rank <= 20 ORDER BY d.structural_height_m DESC, d.dam_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of tallest dams' master article + 20 per-dam Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-14. Universe = top-20 man-made completed dams by structural height (foundation to crest, metres) per the master article's 'Existing' section ranking, with natural landslide/lava dams excluded (the master article's lead foregrounds Jinping-I as 'the tallest man-made dam in the world at 305 m', and the master table's Type column flags Usoi/The Barrier/Lake Waikaremoana as Landslide/Lava — these natural-origin entries are excluded because the Year Completed column does not semantically apply to natural-formation events). temporal_sensitivity = medium because the master ranking shifts as new Chinese mega-dams complete (Lianghekou + Baihetan opened 2021; Yusufeli opened 2022; multiple 200m+ projects under construction). Within the staged 20 rows, three entries are 2020s completions (Lianghekou 2021, Baihetan 2021, Yusufeli 2022) and these rankings may shift within 5-10 years. Per-row Height (m) follows the per-dam Wikipedia article's infobox 'Height' field for the 18 of 20 rows where master-table and per-dam article concur; two exceptions handled by the cycle-2-refined canonical-source rule: (i) Gilgel Gibe III Dam — per-dam article infobox + lead both report 250 m, master-table reports 243 m → staged 250 m per per-dam-wins clause (per-dam article wins when infobox + lead concur and master-table value is unsupported); (ii) Mica Dam — per-dam article is internally inconsistent (infobox 240 m vs body 244 m), master-table reports 243 m → staged 243 m per master-fallback clause (master-table wins when per-dam article does not provide a single internally-consistent value). Per-row Year Completed follows the per-dam article's lead 'completed' / 'opened' / 'first impoundment' year, which differs from the master-table 'Completed' column for 4 rows (Jinping-I 2014 vs master 2013; Yusufeli 2022 vs master 2021; Grande Dixence 1961 vs master 1964; Baihetan 2021 per opening ceremony framing).
_extraction_notes: Factual_lookup instance with secondary top_k category — single-cell-per-row attribute lookup over a top-K-by-physical-dimension fixed entity set. Saturates `factual_lookup` at 5/5 (becomes the 5th fully-cleared category alongside multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5). Source universe = Wikipedia 'List of tallest dams' master article 'Existing' section, filtered to man-made dams (3 natural-origin entries excluded: Usoi 567 m landslide dam Tajikistan 1911, The Barrier 500 m lava dam Canada, Lake Waikaremoana 250 m landslide dam New Zealand). Per-row attribute grounding from 20 per-dam Wikipedia articles (lead/infobox supplies Height, Country, River, Year Completed). Schema: 5 cols (Dam PK + Height (m) numeric + Country categorical + River categorical + Year Completed numeric). Sort: Height (m) DESC primary (tallest-first), Dam ASC alphabetical secondary tiebreaker. Country distribution: China 7 (Jinping-I, Lianghekou, Xiaowan, Baihetan, Xiluodu, Nuozhadu, Laxiwa — dominates modern dam-engineering rankings), Switzerland 2 (Grande Dixence, Mauvoisin — alpine arch dam legacy), Turkey 2 (Yusufeli, Deriner — Çoruh River cascade), singletons for Tajikistan, Georgia, Italy, Mexico, India, Ethiopia, Colombia, Canada, Russia (12 distinct countries from 20 rows). Height range: 242 m (Sayano-Shushenskaya) to 305 m (Jinping-I) — 63 m span across the top-20. Year Completed range: 1957 (Mauvoisin) to 2022 (Yusufeli) — 65 years of major-dam engineering. Cycles 1+2+3 (bridges) lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Dam using Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved ('Gilgel Gibe III Dam' includes the III qualifier; 'Jinping-I' uses hyphen-Roman-numeral per Wikipedia title; 'Chicoasén Dam' uses Spanish acute é per article title); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (master + per-dam), 21 URLs total; (c) man-made-only universe rule explicitly committed at Stage-1 (mirrors the bridges-engineered-only pattern; natural landslide/lava dams excluded because Year Completed does not semantically apply to natural formation events); (d) `source_defined` claim type honestly reflects the top-20-by-master-ranking universe rule; (e) canonical-source rule from cycle-2 bridges applied: per-dam article wins for Main Span/Height/Country/Year when infobox + lead concur and master-table value is unsupported (Gilgel Gibe III 250 m vs master 243 m; Jinping-I 2014 vs master 2013; Yusufeli 2022 vs master 2021; Grande Dixence 1961 vs master 1964); (f) Vajont Dam staged despite 'Disused' operational status post-1963 disaster — structurally completed 1959 (master and article concur); 'disused' is operational status, not completion-status, and Year Completed is the completion-year column not operational-year. Apply Wikipedia common-form naming rule and source-faithful universe definition per PKDB-Bench design philosophy. Entity class: `engineered-structures/dams` (NEW fine-class in the under-represented `engineered-structures` bucket — bucket extends from 2 to 3 instances after this Ready, joining bridges and buildings).
